item.title: After Storm and Wyvern's Ire — A First Session in The Castle Automatic
item.description: A hybrid session report, review and introduction covering the first session of our His Majesty the Worm campaign in The Castle Automatic — the tarot mechanics, the City we built, and a wyvern with lightning breath.

item.title: Rolling for Inspiration
item.description: Random tables give you the answer; I wanted something that just gives me a spark. So I built a generator that serves random lines from public-domain literature, then used it to build a fantasy capital one prompt at a time.

item.title: The Gift of No Content
item.description: Daggerheart has barely any first-party adventure content, and I've come round to thinking that's a good thing. Like early D&D, the gap is letting the community build its own creative tradition.

item.title: Come Into the Woods With Me — A Dolmenwood Retrospective and Review
item.description: A player's retrospective and review on 72 sessions, three characters, and three arcs in Necrotic Gnome's Dolmenwood — the best TTRPG campaign I've played.

item.title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Daggerheart
item.description: A review of Daggerheart and reflections on a thirty-three-session campaign, with thoughts on why the system supports the kind of collaborative, trust-led play I most enjoy.

item.title: How to Win a TTRPG
item.description: A reflection on how Jim Henson's advice about collaboration applies to running and playing TTRPGs, breaking it down into five principles: talent, trust, ideas, space, and invitation. What makes great games isn't system mastery or acting ability, it's building an environment where everyone at the table feels safe to contribute and where those contributions matter.

item.title: On Maps
item.description: A poem about maps in fantasy books, written for Prismatic Wasteland's "the map is not the territory" blog bandwagon.

item.title: Tales of the Valiant after 50 Sessions
item.description: A review of Kobold Press's Tales of the Valiant 5e TTRPG after playing 50 sessions with it. What's in the books, how it plays and whether it is worth switching from D&D

item.title: Jumping on the Quantum Railroad
item.description: The quantum ogre represents everything wrong with railroading: no matter which path players choose, they fight the ogre. But what if it was literally true? Stats for a Tier 2 Daggerheart encounter featuring a probability-warped ogre assassin who exists in multiple quantum states, supported by reality-bending butterflies. Includes full environment features with foreshadowing mechanics. Works as self-aware humor or genuine eldritch threat.

item.title: Year end Review and 2026 Goals
item.description: A look back on my 2025 resolutions and year in gaming and a look forward to next year with goals and accountability
